name: Brave Leo
desc: Privacy-focused integrated assistant. Memory is user-curated: explicit facts and preferences persist across all sessions, stored locally with no server retention. Agentic browsing experiment (Brave Nightly Dec 2025) takes multi-step actions inside sites referencing those preferences.
pricing: Free + paid

name: Browserbase
desc: Cloud browser infrastructure for AI agents. Headless Chromium sessions with persistent cookies, localStorage, session recording — agent workflows carry state across runs. Memory at the session/automation tier rather than conversational.
pricing: Free $0; Developer $20/mo; Startup $99/mo; Scale custom

name: Dia (Atlassian)
desc: The Browser Company's AI-native browser; Atlassian acquired The Browser Company for $610M cash (announced 2025-09, closed 2025-10-21). Stores summaries and preferences locally; opt-in @history feature references up to 7 days of browsing as context. History/chats/bookmarks encrypted local-first.
pricing: Free (no AI); paid AI tiers 'Better Answers' $20/mo (page also shows $10) and 'Better Days' $100/mo

name: Fellou
desc: Silicon Valley. Spatial agentic browser with explicit Agentic Memory layer learning from history and notes for instant recall of past research sessions. Operates on logged-in accounts (Quora, X, etc.); runs tasks while user is idle.
pricing: Free (1,000-Spark bonus); Plus $19/mo; Pro $39.90/mo; Ultra $199.90/mo (annual ~20% off)

name: Microsoft Edge Copilot Mode + Journeys (now Copilot in Edge)
desc: Copilot Mode retired 2026-05-13; its features now ship as Copilot in Edge. Journeys clusters browsing history into topic cards on the new tab page (desktop, and US mobile); Copilot long-term memory can reference past chats and browsing history with user controls; agentic 'Browse with Copilot' (formerly Copilot Actions) for US Microsoft 365 Premium.
pricing: Free in Edge (Journeys free on desktop in English markets); Browse with Copilot requires Microsoft 365 Premium (US); M365 Personal/Family/Premium get extended u

name: Opera AI (formerly Aria)
desc: Memory feature stores user-declared preferences and facts; injected into future prompts. Understands current tab content; manages open tabs contextually. Memory off by default, end-user controlled, stored alongside the prompt rather than the LLM.
pricing: Free (included with Opera browser); Opera One Pro has additional AI credits

name: Perplexity Comet
desc: AI-native Chromium-based browser. Assistant operates across tabs and sessions; persistent memory of preferences; multi-step agentic tasks without leaving the browser. Memory is opt-in and server-side; enterprise memory tier separately available.
pricing: Free (since Oct 2025); optional Comet Plus $5/mo; Perplexity Pro $20/mo / Max $200/mo

name: Sigma (Private AI Browser)
desc: Chromium-based browser with AI agent (navigates pages, fills forms), chat-with-page, deep research and an in-browser local LLM (Eclipse) for private on-device processing; macOS, Windows, iOS, Android beta.
pricing: Free $0; Plus $10/mo ($8 annual); Pro $75/mo ($60 annual)

name: Anthropic Auto Dream
desc: Unconfirmed / experimental — described only by third-party reports, not Anthropic docs: a background Claude Code sub-agent that periodically scans ~/.claude/projects/‹project›/memory/ plus recent transcripts, prunes stale notes, deduplicates, resolves contradictions, converts relative dates to absolute ones and rewrites MEMORY.md; reportedly triggers after 24+ hours and 5+ sessions, or manually vi
deployment: Local CLI (Claude Code) — Claude.ai web not in scope
pricing: bundled with Claude Code (no separate fee)

name: Claude Code auto-memory
desc: Persistent file-based memory at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ with a MEMORY.md index plus typed memory files (user / feedback / project / reference). Loaded into context across sessions.
deployment: not applicable — not a deployable product
pricing: not applicable — not commercial

name: Claude-CursorMemoryMCP
desc: FastAPI server. RBAC + API-key auth, encryption, backup/recovery, embedding pipeline with deduplication. Only server in this list with role-based access control over pgvector.
pricing: free / open source

name: Cognee MCP
desc: "Cognify" extracts entities and relationships into a structured graph. Saves interaction patterns as coding rules; uses both vector and graph DBs. Bundled in Cognee v0.3.5+.
deployment: self-hosted (local vector + graph DB); cloud option exists (topoteretes managed)
pricing: OSS (Apache-2.0) self-hosted; Cognee Cloud managed service (pricing not on README); some production components (Postgres graph store) are licensed products

name: Graphiti MCP Server (Zep)
desc: Tracks how facts change over time; maintains provenance; supports prescribed and learned ontology. Bi-temporal edges (when known vs when valid). Only server that distinguishes "fact learned" from "fact true."
deployment: cloud (Zep managed) or self-hosted via Graphiti OSS + Neo4j/local graph DB
pricing: free tier: 2500 messages/mo + 2.5MB graph data; paid: $1.25/1000 messages + $2.50/MB extra; Enterprise custom

name: Hindsight MCP
desc: World (facts), Experiences (agent actions), Opinion (beliefs with confidence scores), Observation (mental models). Entity resolution ("Alice" and "my coworker Alice" same node). Mimics human recall topology.
pricing: OSS self-hosted free; Hindsight Cloud usage-based with free starter credits

name: Mem0 MCP (official)
desc: Archived 2026-03-24 (read-only); README now points to Mem0's official cloud-hosted MCP server at mcp.mem0.ai/mcp. Mem0's managed cloud API exposed as MCP tools. Semantic search + CRUD on memories scoped by user / agent / session. Cloud-hosted MCP endpoint — no local infrastructure required.
deployment: superseded — use Mem0's hosted MCP endpoint (mcp.mem0.ai/mcp) or the mem0-mcp-server PyPI package
pricing: free tier (Hobby: 10K memories 1K retrieval/mo); Starter $19/mo; Pro $249/mo (graph memory included); Enterprise custom
type: Hybrid vector + graph via cloud API

name: Official MCP Memory server
desc: Knowledge-graph-based persistent memory MCP server — the canonical reference implementation. npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory ; configurable via MEMORY_FILE_PATH .
deployment: local (Node.js MCP server; local JSON file)
pricing: free / open source (Apache-2.0 / MIT)
license: Apache-2.0 AND MIT (new contributions Apache-2.0; legacy code MIT; docs CC-BY-4.

name: OpenMemory MCP
desc: Mem0's MCP memory layer for coding agents (Claude, Cursor, VS Code etc.). Ships both as a hosted service (API key + npx installer) and a local Docker-based self-hosted server where data stays on-machine.
deployment: not applicable — not a deployable product
pricing: not applicable — not commercial

name: Superpowers episodic-memory plugin
desc: Claude Code plugin that indexes prior conversations at session end and exposes search/show tools via MCP. Distributed via obra/superpowers-marketplace ; install with /plugin install episodic-memory@superpowers-marketplace .
deployment: local — runs as Claude Code plugin via superpowers marketplace; no cloud component
pricing: free / open source (MIT); no paid tier

name: claude-brain
desc: Claude Code plugin packaging of Memvid (see Dedicated memory layers). Wraps the Memvid .mv2 single-file store as a slash-command-installable plugin so per-project memory becomes a git-committable file inside the repo.
pricing: free / open source

name: claude-mem
desc: Hooks into Claude Code's session lifecycle; compresses tool outputs into ~500-token observations via Claude's agent SDK. SQLite + FTS5 with optional Chroma vector. "Endless Mode" compresses in-flight to extend session length. Captures what the agent did , not just what the user typed.
deployment: local — SQLite + FTS5 per project; optional Chroma vector; no cloud
pricing: free / open source (Apache-2.0); no paid tier

name: claude-supermemory
desc: Wraps Supermemory cloud API. Team memory shared across project members, separate from personal memories. Auto-capture on session end; per-repo config.
deployment: Supermemory cloud API by default (API key); local self-host option via npx supermemory local
pricing: requires Supermemory Pro (pricing not publicly listed; contact sales)

name: codebase-memory-mcp (DeusData)
desc: High-performance MCP server building persistent code knowledge graphs via AST. 155 languages via vendored tree-sitter; SQLite + WAL; single static binary; zero runtime deps. Knowledge graph: Project/Package/File/Module/Class/Function/Method/Interface/Enum/Type/Route/Resource nodes; CALLS/IMPORTS/DEFINES/IMPLEMENTS/INHERITS/HTTP_CALLS/ASYNC_CALLS/EMITS/LISTENS_ON/DATA_FLOWS/SIMILAR_TO/SEMANTICALLY_
deployment: Local — single static binary (macOS arm64/amd64; Linux arm64/amd64; Windows amd64)
pricing: free / open source (MIT); no paid tier

name: engram
desc: SQLite + FTS5; agent decides what to save (not firehose capture). Single Go binary, no CGO, no Node/Python/Docker dependencies. HTTP API + MCP + CLI + TUI; optional cloud sync with local-source-of-truth.
deployment: local — single Go binary with SQLite/FTS5; MCP stdio, works with any MCP agent
pricing: free / open source (MIT)

name: local-memory-mcp
desc: SQLite + FTS5 + BM25 ranking. Stores learnings, decisions with reasoning and alternatives , entities, observations. Loads context from last 3 sessions. Only server that captures why a decision was made + alternatives considered.
deployment: local — SQLite + FTS5; zero cloud dependency; no API keys required
pricing: free / open source (MIT); no paid tier

name: mcp-knowledge-graph
desc: KG-based local fork of @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory . Avoids ephemeral npx installs; supports named databases for topic scoping; user-controlled memory path. Drop-in for teams that want the official KG model without npx churn.
deployment: local (Node.js MCP server; local JSON file storage)
pricing: free / open source (MIT)
type: Stable local fork of official MCP memory

name: mcp-memory (Puliczek)
desc: Embeddings via @cf/baai/bge-m3 ; Vectorize + D1; per-user namespace isolation. Runs entirely on Cloudflare Workers — no separate server.
deployment: serverless — Cloudflare Workers + Vectorize + D1; one-click Cloudflare deploy
pricing: free — Cloudflare free tier: 1k memories / ~28k queries per month; no paid tier

name: mcp-memory-service (doobidoo)
desc: SQLite-Vec default, Cloudflare hybrid for production. Typed edges (causes, fixes, contradicts). Autonomous consolidation compresses old memories. SSE real-time notifications + D3.js visualisation dashboard. Agent-pipeline focused (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen).
deployment: Local/self-hosted — SQLite-vec local; Cloudflare, Hybrid or Milvus backends; no managed cloud
pricing: free / open source (Apache-2.0); no paid tier

name: Aider
desc: Appends conversation turns to .aider.chat.history.md in project root. restore_chat_history defaults to false — no automatic replay into new sessions. Community /session save command for JSON state snapshots. .aider.conf.yml carries static preferences.
pricing: OSS
type: Per-repo chat history file + YAML config

name: Augment Code
desc: Real-time knowledge graph indexed from connected repos + commit history + CI/CD + tickets + docs. Separate Agent Memory layer (Sept 2025) captures session decisions/corrections/goals as discrete items with developer review/approval UI. MCP endpoint exposes the graph.
pricing: Standard $20/mo (incl. $20 usage, up to 50 seats); Business $100/mo (incl. $100 usage); Enterprise custom
type: Real-time semantic Context Engine + curated Agent Memory

name: Beads (Steve Yegge)
desc: Dolt-backed, dependency-aware graph issue tracker that acts as persistent structured memory for coding agents, replacing markdown plans; `bd remember` stores durable facts and `bd prime` re-injects them. Traction: ~28k GitHub stars
pricing: searched not found

name: Bolt.new (StackBlitz)
desc: In-browser WebContainer (Rust-backed shared memory) is the implicit state store. No dedicated memory abstraction — project files are the state. Team plan adds shared workspaces + GitHub integration.
pricing: Free 1M tokens/mo (300k/day); Pro $25/mo 10M tokens; Teams $30/member/mo; Enterprise custom

name: Continue.dev Memory MCP
desc: Discontinued: Continue was bought by Cursor (announced ~2026-06-16); the product is discontinued and the continuedev/continue repo is read-only. Official Memory MCP (Mar 2025) backed by a knowledge graph. Memory is injected via MCP rather than native to the Continue core. Scope depends on MCP server deployment (local or shared).
deployment: Both (VS Code/JetBrains extension local + optional shared MCP server)
pricing: Free (OSS core); paid Continue Hub plans for teams (pricing on website)

name: Cursor Memories
desc: Project-scoped memories in Cursor, created either by a background 'sidecar' model watching chats or by the agent via tool calls, and managed as auto-generated rules in settings. Traction: First-party feature of one of the most widely used AI IDEs
pricing: searched not found

name: Devin (Cognition)
desc: Structured Knowledge items stored server-side. Three-tier scope: repo-pinned (always injected), global (recall by relevance), org/enterprise (visible to org members). Auto-generates Repo Knowledge from repo structure each session; reads past session trajectories for self-improvement; writes notes for recurring scheduled tasks.
pricing: Free $0; Pro $20/mo; Max $200/mo; Teams $80/mo; Enterprise custom

name: Gemini CLI memory (save_memory / GEMINI.md)
desc: Google's open-source Gemini CLI persists facts by editing tiered Markdown memory files — repo GEMINI.md, a per-project private memory folder and global ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md — that load into hierarchical context each session. Traction: Google first-party; Gemini CLI is one of the most-used terminal coding agents
pricing: searched not found

name: GitHub Copilot Memory (agentic memory)
desc: Repository-scoped memories that Copilot coding agent, code review and CLI write automatically, share across features, validate against the current code before use, and expire after 28 days; owners can review/delete them. Traction: Shipped to all paid GitHub Copilot plans; default-on for Pro/Pro+
pricing: searched not found

name: Letta Code
desc: Letta's stateful coding-agent harness: agents rewrite their own memory blocks and skills, version context in git via MemFS (syncable to GitHub) and reflect via a periodic /sleeptime 'dreaming' process. Traction: ~3.5k stars; from Letta (MemGPT) team
pricing: searched not found

name: Lovable
desc: Long-term context stored as files in /docs that the agent reads on each session. Agent Mode (default since July 2025) holds working context within session but doesn't persist cross-session beyond filesystem state.
deployment: Managed (editor/agent are Lovable-hosted); Enterprise private preview runs generated apps + data plane in customer AWS/Azure account
pricing: Free + paid

name: Mistral Vibe (Remote Agents) + Mistral Medium 3.5
desc: Vibe is Mistral's cloud-hosted coding-agent platform: each session runs in an isolated sandbox with task state, history, and approvals. Spawnable from CLI or Le Chat, with parallel execution. Local CLI sessions can be "teleported" to the cloud and resumed. Powered by Mistral Medium 3.5 (77.6% SWE-Bench Verified). Plugs into GitHub, Linear/Jira, Sentry, Slack/Teams.
deployment: Managed cloud (la Plateforme + Le Chat) + NVIDIA NIM containers
pricing: API: $1.5/M input tokens; $7.5/M output tokens (Medium 3.5); Vibe via Pro/Team/Enterprise plans
type: Cloud-hosted async coding agents with teleportable session state

name: OpenAI Codex (cloud agent)
desc: Memory under ~/.codex/memories/ : summaries, durable entries, recent-input logs, supporting evidence — generated in background after sessions go idle. Chronicle (opt-in macOS preview) uses screen-capture to seed memory. Off by default; opt-in via config.toml .
deployment: Both (cloud agent via ChatGPT platform + CLI tool local)
pricing: Included in ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Business/Edu/Enterprise plans (memory feature)

name: OpenAI Codex Memories + Chronicle
desc: Codex Memories carries preferences, conventions and pitfalls across Codex threads as local Markdown files; Chronicle (research preview) adds screen-aware memory by having background agents summarize periodic Mac screen captures into those memory files. Traction: OpenAI first-party feature for Codex app (ChatGPT Pro, macOS at launch); wide press coverage
pricing: searched not found

name: Replit Agent
desc: No documented built-in persistent semantic memory store. Session duration expanded to 200 min (Agent 3); Agent 4 shifts toward persistent runtimes. Temporal used for orchestration durability, not semantic memory. Cross-session memory relies on filesystem + agent-written notes.
pricing: Starter free; Core $20/mo ($18 annual); Pro $100/mo ($90 annual); Enterprise custom

name: Serena (Oraios)
desc: LSP-backed MCP coding toolkit ('IDE for your agent') with a built-in project memory system for sharing knowledge across sessions, users and projects alongside AGENTS.md. Traction: ~30k GitHub stars
pricing: searched not found

name: Sweep AI
desc: Superseded: the sweepai/sweep README says the team now builds an AI coding assistant for JetBrains; the GitHub-app product described here is no longer the focus (repo not archived). No dedicated persistent memory layer. Operates as a GitHub App — reads issue + codebase fresh on each trigger. Some context implicit in the PR/issue threads it created previously.
deployment: Both (GitHub App managed + JetBrains plugin local)
pricing: Free (community); Pro and Team tiers; LLM cost + 5% markup model for agent usage
license: proprietary (Sweep Enterprise Edition License; some parts MIT)

name: Tabnine
desc: Enterprise Context Engine builds a multi-dimensional knowledge graph from repos + CI/CD + PRs + tickets + docs at the org level. Individual completions stay session-scoped. Tabnine Agents (Nov 2025) adds team-shared agent context.
pricing: No free tier; Code Assistant $39/user/mo, Agentic Platform $59/user/mo (annual); Headless Agents add-on $1.2k–5k/mo

name: agentmemory (rohitg00)
desc: Self-hosted persistent memory layer that captures coding-agent activity and recalls it in later sessions, positioned on public benchmark results. Traction: ~29k GitHub stars; #7 in TeleAI Awesome-Agent-Memory
pricing: searched not found

name: context-mode
desc: MCP server + hooks that sandbox tool output out of the coding agent's context window (claims ~98% reduction) and persist session memory across 17 agent platforms. Traction: ~32k GitHub stars
pricing: searched not found

name: memsearch (Zilliz)
desc: Zilliz's persistent memory layer shared across agents like Claude Code and Codex: Markdown files are the source of truth, and Milvus indexes them for search. Traction: ~2.7k stars; from the Milvus vendor
pricing: searched not found

name: AI Singapore SEA-LION
desc: SEA-LION-Embedding (March 2026): retrieval + reranking models contrastively trained on 245M text pairs across 10 SE Asian languages. SEA-BED benchmark (169 datasets). SEA-LION v4 (Gemma-based) at 128K context with native function calling.
deployment: Both (free download self-hosted + Amazon SageMaker JumpStart for managed deployment)
pricing: Free download (Hugging Face + AISG website); no commercial pricing

name: Acontext (memodb)
desc: 'Agent Skills as a Memory Layer': an open-source skill-memory layer that stores what agents learn as agent skill files. Built by the Memobase team. Traction: ~3.7k stars
pricing: searched not found

name: Aleph Alpha PhariaAI / PhariaCatch
desc: German enterprise stack. PhariaCatch captures + preserves organisational knowledge through structured human-machine collaboration; PhariaAssistant queries via semantic search. Combines sovereign deployment constraints with explainability tooling.
deployment: Managed cloud (STACKIT EU) or on-prem enterprise deployment
pricing: Enterprise only (PhariaAI is an enterprise stack; no public pricing)

name: Anda Hippocampus (now Anda Brain)
desc: Renamed Anda Brain (repo now ldclabs/anda-brain). Native graph-based memory for autonomous AI agents. Bio-inspired sleep-based memory consolidation.
deployment: Self-hosted on-premises (full data privacy; no cloud service)
pricing: OSS (Apache-2.0 + MIT); free — no commercial pricing
